rules.rule: Check for urgent signs at initial assessment of the patient
rules.problem: Type (check task) and red-box coverage are right (all 20 red-box items present), but the task's title claims every item is an urgent sign while three items (Cough, Unable to sit up, Diabetes mellitus known present) come from the Management line or the routine-tests block, not the red box. Cough is also a recorded common symptom and need not be checked for. Trigger on the root 'Clinical finding' is a broad approximation of 'every patient'.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure glucose if decreased consciousness, seizures, confused, unable to sit up or diabetic
rules.problem: Conditions and or-structure match the Management line exactly. Note the house brief treats glucose as a routine vital needing no measure task; a conditional task is a defensible exception.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure respiratory rate and oxygen saturation if coughing or difficulty breathing
rules.problem: Matches the routine-tests block ('If coughing/difficulty breathing, also check respiratory rate and oxygen saturation'); 'if available' is dropped, which is unavoidable.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure MUAC and height in the pregnant patient
rules.problem: Trigger right; the page limits MUAC and height to the booking visit, and the rule has no timing, so it is due at every antenatal visit. The booking-visit Hb, rapid rhesus/syphilis, urine dipstick and conditional fingerprick glucose (risk factors in footnote 2) are not encoded, nor the 26-week glucose and 30/36-week Hb.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure BMI inputs, waist circumference and glucose in the patient with hypertension
rules.problem: Trigger right. 'Check once a year' timing (and 3-6 monthly if trying to lose weight) is dropped for all three measurements; the yearly urine dipstick and the 'also check glucose if glucose on urine dipstick' condition are not encoded.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure glucose, BMI inputs, waist and hip circumference in the patient with diabetes
rules.problem: Trigger right and every-visit glucose right. The yearly timing for BMI, waist circumference and waist-hip ratio is dropped (so they are due every visit alongside glucose); yearly urine dipstick and visual acuity, and the every-visit 'urine dipstick only if fingerprick glucose >= 11.1' are not encoded.

Type and level right: 'Give urgent attention' justifies Urgent. All 20 red-box items present; 'Headache and vomiting' is correctly an `and`, 'Pregnant with abdominal pain/vaginal bleeding' is correctly and/or, RR >= 30 is correct. No presenting-complaint `and` wrapper is correct because the page applies to every patient.

rules.rule: (missing) Prompt review: 'Ensure the patient with any of the following is seen promptly by nurse or doctor'
rules.problem: The page's second triage block (BP >= 180/110 or systolic < 80; pregnant with BP >= 140/90; pulse irregular, >= 100 or < 50; temperature >= 38; RR >= 30; glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) or >= 11.1; SpO2 < 92% at rest or drop to < 87% on exertion) has no priority evaluation at all. These are all measurement comparisons the grammar can express. This is the page's main triage logic outside the red box and it is absent.

summary: The biggest gap is a missing rule, not a wrong one: the 'seen promptly by nurse or doctor' block (BP >= 180/110 or systolic < 80, pregnant BP >= 140/90, pulse irregular/>= 100/< 50, temperature >= 38, glucose < 3 or < 4 if diabetic or >= 11.1, SpO2 < 92% at rest or < 87% on exertion) is not encoded as a priority evaluation although every item is a measurement comparison the grammar supports. The red box itself is encoded faithfully: all 20 danger signs are present in both the check_for and the Urgent priority evaluation with the right and/or structure, every SNOMED concept resolves, and 'Confused' is a direct synonym of Clouded consciousness. Lesser issues: the 'urgent signs' check_for also lists Cough, Unable to sit up and known diabetes, which come from the routine-tests and Management lines rather than the red box; and the pregnant, hypertension and diabetes measure tasks drop the page's timing (booking visit / once a year) so they fall due at every visit.
